operational_end_state.success_condition: Resolve the assigned strategic sites across the campaign region under supreme command; control of the strategic anchor alone is not equivalent to securing the whole region.
operational_end_state.war_termination_rule: Political war termination, annexation, treaty terms, and follow-on territorial settlement remain separate sovereign and diplomatic decisions.

Of these, 5,000 are Qin-assigned troops and 4,500 are House or retinue troops accompanying under Tang Wei's own authority. Other Qin forces on the campaign roster: 73,200 troops organized under 3 primary command(s), under Kanki, Mou Gou, Ousen, at Sanyou, task: concentrate Mou Gou, Ousen, and Kanki field forces for the northern Wei campaign; 46,100 troops organized under 2 primary command(s), under Ouki, Tou, at Keiyou, task: concentrate Ouki and Tou field forces for the northern Wei campaign; 40,000 troops organized under 1 primary command(s), under Mou Bu, at Qin Southern March, task: hold Mou Bu's shock army ready for the northern Wei campaign; 5,000 troops represented by 1 aggregate field body/bodies, under Fan Yi, at Sanyou, task: maintain the Qin mobile reserve as a participant in the northern Wei campaign; 3,000 troops represented by 1 aggregate field body/bodies, under Shou Hei Kun, at Qin Eastern Military Depot, task: maintain the eastern reserve as a participant in the northern Wei campaign. Combined Qin strength on the current campaign roster is 176,800. The staff designate Sanyou as the present operational area. Qin has authorized entry into the target state, and the field command has completed arrival and deployment at Sanyou; any further maneuver requires a follow-on lawful order or Tang Wei's own lawful initiative. Intelligence estimate: an official estimate of roughly 88,000-147,000 troops able to influence the theater; 7 distinct opposing field body/bodies reported; opposing commanders: Gai Mou, Huan Zhen, Qiao Jie, Deng Shan, Go Hou Mei, Jing Rong, Rei Ou; no confirmed battle contact. These are staff estimates. A reported enemy field body is not assumed to have the same internal echelon structure as one of Tang Wei's tactical leaf formations. The Bureau's standing orders record arrival and deployment at Sanyou as complete. Any further maneuver or battle commitment requires a follow-on lawful basis; this completed order does not direct another march to the same location.
